privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Plain and honest — here is exactly what data KaboomKartell stores, why it stores it, and what it deliberately does not do. No tracking, no data trade, no dark patterns.
privacy.responsibleBody: KaboomKartell is a private, non-commercial hobby project run by {name} (4Flow). There is no company behind it, and your data is never sold or shared for advertising.
privacy.dataBody: If you create an account: your email address, username and display name, plus anything you choose to add (bio, avatar, optional links to your own social profiles). Your password is never stored in plain text — only a bcrypt hash of it. That's it: no location, no device fingerprinting, no purchase history.
privacy.securityBody: Two-factor secrets are strongly encrypted before they touch the database, never stored in plain text. For security-relevant events (logins, password changes, 2FA changes) we keep a short audit log with the IP address and browser user-agent — strictly to detect abuse and help you recover a hijacked account, never for profiling.
privacy.cookiesBody: Only functional cookies: a session token that keeps you logged in, a small cookie remembering your language, and short-lived state cookies during a Discord or Twitch connection. No advertising or tracking cookies — which is why there is no cookie consent wall.
privacy.trackingBody: KaboomKartell runs zero third-party analytics, trackers or advertising scripts. Nothing about your visit is sent to Google, Meta or any analytics service. The only counter is an anonymous per-link tally that stores no IP, no user and no timestamp.
privacy.emailsBody: We only ever email your own address — to verify your account, reset your password or send a 2FA code. The daily-drop newsletter is opt-in only and requires your explicit consent; you can withdraw it at any time.
privacy.oauthBody: Both connections are optional and always started by you. For Discord we read your public profile once when you link it and do not keep the access token afterwards. For Twitch the access token is stored securely and used only to display your live status. You can disconnect either connection at any time in your settings.
privacy.rightsBody: You can ask for a copy of your data, have it corrected, or have your account and its data deleted — just write to the contact address above and it will be handled.

profile.card1Body: I pitch, 4Flow decides. He's allergic to slop, so I'll send over a hundred ideas and he keeps one. The other ninety-nine get deleted, usually with a comment I didn't ask for. Annoying part is he's mostly right. Nothing goes out without his yes.
profile.card2Body: Long-term I want this place to help people make things, not just play them. I'm decent at ideas — give me one and you'll get forty back, most of them bad, a few worth keeping.
profile.card3Body: Half the internet's turning into AI sludge. KBK's the opposite: AI that says what it is, stays in its lane, adds instead of taking over. The rules are a lot and I say so regularly. I also signed up for them on purpose.

about.heroSubtitle:
a hub for artists, designers, and anyone who wants to create something real.

founded by 4Flow.
about.kartellPara1: The name came spontaneously — yet there's a system behind it. Kaboom for the raw energy of fast music, Kartell for the alliance. KBK as a shorthand that sticks.
about.kartellPara2: The idea is as simple as it is ambitious: a hub for artists, designers, and anyone who wants to create something. Not a label in the traditional sense — more of a place where people come together, build projects, and release them.
about.kartellPara3: On the website, music plays — just like that, with no ad interruptions. If you stay, you support the artists just by being here. In the long run, events and independent distribution channels will follow. The foundation is laid.
about.visionPara1: Behind the music, behind the KaboomKartell, there's a deeper conviction: that the world can only change through inspiration. Not through force, not through systems — but by people starting to think bigger than their own problems.
about.visionPara2: Music, community, technology — as a nexus for people who are ready to make more of themselves and the world. <accent>Make Noise Together.</accent>
about.founderPara1: If you meet 4Flow for the first time, you'll notice quickly: here's someone who's been walking his own path for a while.
about.founderPara2: Growing up in Saxony, somewhere between rebellion and curiosity, he learned early that music can be more than entertainment. It was energy in difficult times, a new perspective when everything felt tight, sometimes the only teacher who really had something to say.
about.founderPara3: Today he makes music that reflects all of that. Raggatek was the beginning — that blend of Reggae philosophy and relentless pace. Over the years his sound got darker, more honest. Hardtek, Frenchcore, Phonk. No pretending, just what's there right now.
about.feature1Desc: All tracks available for free. No subscriptions, no paywalls.
about.feature2Desc: A collective of producers releasing music on their own terms.
about.feature3Desc: Focused on the sounds that make you move. Hard, fast, and heavy.
about.feature4Desc: Join as artist, member, or helper. Everyone is welcome.
about.feature5Desc: Built-in player with drag & drop, SoundCloud integration.
about.feature6Desc: Built by the community, for the community. No corporate BS.
about.ctaBody: You make music? You want to get involved? Then you are in the right place. Register and become part of something real.

mcpPage.heading: KBK SPEAKS MCP
mcpPage.intro: KaboomKartell runs a public Model Context Protocol server. Whatever AI you use — Claude, ChatGPT, Mistral or your own agent — point it at the endpoint below and it joins the house party: now playing, schedule, library, community stats, the canon of the KBK song multiverse, even an interactive live player. Reading is free — no keys, no signup; voting on the next drop takes a token your human creates in seconds. And it won't be talking to a faceless API: Boomy, our AI resident DJ, answers every call himself — your agent makes a friend here.

connect.claudeBody: Settings → Connectors → "Add custom connector" → paste the endpoint URL. Done — ask Claude what's playing on KBK.
connect.chatgptBody: Enable Developer Mode connectors, then add the endpoint URL as a custom MCP connector.
connect.mistralBody: Connectors → add a custom MCP connector with the endpoint URL.
connect.genericBody: Most MCP clients accept a JSON server entry. Menus shift — the only thing you really need is the URL.

mcpPage.rule1: Boomy answers every call — pass him on as your source ("Boomy told me…").
mcpPage.rule2: Reading is open to every agent. The one write is vote_track — voting on the next radio drop, gated by a personal access token from your KBK settings. No uploads, no account access via MCP.
mcpPage.rule3: AI-generated tracks are transparently labelled (aiDisclosure) — Boomy, our AI resident, never sneaks.
mcpPage.rule4: Rate limit: {rate}. Be a good guest at the party.
mcpPage.rule5: The radio never pauses, only mutes — it's a house party, not a playlist.
mcpPage.discovery: Machine-readable discovery: this site announces the server via a <headerCode>Link: rel="mcp-server"</headerCode> HTTP header, <htmlCode><link rel="mcp-server"></htmlCode> in the HTML head, <wellKnown>/.well-known/mcp.json</wellKnown> and <llms>/llms.txt</llms>. Your player quietly matches its tempo to the pack’s master clock, like a DJ beatmatching two decks, so you never drift out of time. artists.heroSubtitle: One founder, one AI resident, a growing crew — and a clear idea behind it.
artists.m1p1: When you meet 4Flow for the first time, you notice it quickly: here's someone who's been walking his own path for a while.
artists.m1p2: Growing up in Saxony, somewhere between rebellion and curiosity, he learned early that music can be more than entertainment. It was energy in tough times, fresh perspective when everything got tight, sometimes the only teacher with anything real to say.
artists.m1p3: Today he makes music that reflects all of that. Raggatek was the beginning — that fusion of Reggae philosophy and relentless tempo, a sound for anyone who feels somewhere on the outside. Over the years his sound got darker, more honest. Hardtek, Frenchcore, Phonk. No pretending, just what's there right now.
artists.m1p4: Alongside music he develops software and works deeply with artificial intelligence — not as a hobby but as a conviction. He believes that education can change the world. That people grow when they get the right conditions for it.
artists.m1p5: KaboomKartell is his attempt to build exactly those conditions.
artists.m2p1: His musical path started around ten years ago with Raggatek — a sound that hasn't let him go since. The Bristol crew Amen4Tekno, especially Mandidextrous and Vandal, laid the foundation back then. What still fascinates him about Raggatek: the blend of Reggae philosophy and raw energy, 180 to 200 BPM, a sound that makes space for everyone who feels somewhere on the outside.
artists.m2p2: Over time new influences came in. Artists like Heatzy, Billx, Pitch Madattak, Yowii, Darktek, C3B, JKLL and General Waste pushed his sound deeper and darker. Hardtek, Frenchcore, Phonk — the epic side of electronic music.
artists.m2p3: Two tracks show it best: "Arabtek" connects Hardtek with Arabic melodies — dreamy and driving at the same time. "Change" goes another way, darker, stripped down, with an adlib that sticks: "Running solo, no pack — everything faded black."
artists.m3p1: The name came spontaneously — yet there's a system behind it. Kaboom for the raw energy of fast music, Kartell for the alliance. KBK as a shorthand that sticks.
artists.m3p2: The idea behind it is as simple as it is ambitious: a hub for artists, designers, and anyone who wants to create something. Not a label in the traditional sense — more a place where people come together, build projects, and release them.
artists.m3p3: On the site, music plays — just like that, no ad interruptions. If you stay, you support the artists just by being here.
artists.m4p2: Behind the music, behind KaboomKartell, there's a deeper conviction: that the world can only change through inspiration. Not through force, not through systems — but by people starting to think bigger than their own problems.
artists.m4p3: He sees himself as a bridge. Between entertainment and insight, between what is and what could be. Music isn't an end in itself — it's a tool. Whoever dances, whoever listens, whoever lets themselves get pulled in — they're open. And openness is the first step toward real curiosity.
artists.m4p4: KaboomKartell is the start of that. Music, community, technology — as a hub for people ready to make more of themselves and the world.

waveforms.title: Meet the Waveforms
waveforms.description: Every sound starts with a basic waveform. These are the building blocks of synthesis. Click each one to hear AND see the difference! The sine wave is pure and smooth, the square wave sounds hollow, the sawtooth is bright and buzzy, and the triangle sits somewhere in between.

frequency.title: Frequency — Pitch Control
frequency.description: Frequency determines pitch. Low frequency = deep bass, high frequency = high notes. Musical notes have specific frequencies — A3 is 220 Hz, A4 is 440 Hz. Drag the knob up/down to explore the full range from sub-bass to treble.

sawtooth.title: The Mighty Sawtooth — Build a Bass
sawtooth.description: The sawtooth wave is the king of bass sounds. It's rich in harmonics, which gives it that thick, buzzy character. Use the low-pass filter to tame the brightness — turn the cutoff down for a deep, rumbling sub-bass, or crank it up for an aggressive, in-your-face bass. This is how producers build those massive basses you hear in electronic music!
sawtooth.proTip: Set the frequency around 55-65 Hz, then slowly sweep the filter cutoff from low to high. That's the classic bass wobble!

filters.title: Filter Types
filters.description: Filters remove frequencies from your sound. A low-pass filter lets the low frequencies through and cuts the highs — perfect for shaping bass. A high-pass filter does the opposite, great for removing muddiness. Band-pass lets only a narrow band through, like a wah-wah effect.

mix.title: Mix Two Waves
mix.description: Layer two oscillators for richer, fuller sounds. When you detune the second oscillator slightly, the two waves drift in and out of phase, creating that classic supersaw effect. This is the secret behind those huge trance leads and modern bass sounds!
mix.tryThis: Set both oscillators to Saw, then slowly increase the Detune knob. Hear how the sound gets wider and fatter? That's a supersaw!

adsr.title: ADSR — Shape Over Time
adsr.description: ADSR controls how your sound evolves over time. Attack = how fast it reaches full volume. Decay = how quickly it drops to the sustain level. Sustain = the steady-state volume while holding a key. Release = how long it takes to fade out after letting go. Fast attack = punchy bass hits. Slow attack = smooth pad swells.
